claims.text: The first traffic signal, installed outside the Houses of Parliament in London in December 1868, used red and green gas lamps at night.
The 1868 signal was not lit by electric bulbs, oil lamps or candles.
By day, a police officer operated the signal's semaphore arms by hand.
In January 1869 the gas-lit signal exploded, injuring the policeman operating it.
The signal was removed, and traffic signals were not used in London again for decades.
